facts.fact: MyJoyOnline says Ghana's Cybersecurity Act, 2020 (Act 1038), covering impersonation, fraud and other cyber offences, can be applied to AI-assisted crimes such as voice cloning and manipulated videos used in scams, though it does not regulate AI itself.
MyJoyOnline says the Ghana Police Service arrested eleven individuals, including Nigerian nationals, in May 2026 after a deepfake video of President Mahama was spread on social media.

GHA.note: Nothing on government use of AI.

facts.fact: MyJoyOnline says Ghana currently has no standalone law specifically regulating artificial intelligence.

GHA.note: Nothing on AI in a sector's public system.
Nothing on AI built or hosted in the country.

facts.fact: MyJoyOnline names Ghana's Cybersecurity Act, 2020 (Act 1038) as existing law covering impersonation, fraud and other cyber-related offences.

GHA.note: The May 2026 deepfake arrests are not said to be under the Act, so no use is recorded.
The May 2026 arrests concern a deepfake video, not stated speech about the government; not recorded as punishment.
